LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv . For more information, please contact the City Clerk''s office at (949) 724-6205.
ADJOURNMENT
At 11:00 p.m., the City Council will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be considered and acted upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional time is required until a future City Council meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are on file with the City Clerk and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 12 days prior to a regular City Council meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org at least 12 days prior to the scheduled City Council meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv .
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL RECEIVED AFTER THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA
Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk''s Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUBMITTAL OF INFORMATION BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC FOR DISSEMINATION OR PRESENTATION AT PUBLIC MEETINGS
Media Types and Guidelines
Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.
MEETING SCHEDULE

MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING

  February 9, 2021
  City Council Chamber
  One Civic Center Plaza
  Irvine, CA 92606

CALL TO ORDER
The regular meeting of the Irvine City Council was called to order at 4:20 p.m. on February
9, 2021, in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine,
California; Mayor Khan presiding.
ROLL CALL
  Present: 5 Councilmember  Larry Agran*
  Councilmember  Mike Carroll
  Councilmember  Anthony Kuo
  Vice Mayor  Tammy Kim
  Mayor  Farrah N. Khan
  *Via teleconference

Mayor Khan announced that the meeting was broadcast live on Cox Communications
Local Access Channel 30 and AT&T U-Verse Channel 99, and livestreamed online at
cityofirvine.org; and that in an effort to protect public health and prevent the spread of
COVID-19, members of the public had the ability to provide live comments on agenda
items using Zoom. She also noted that the e-comment feature had been extended for all
agenda items, which allowed members of the public the ability to submit e-comments on
all agenda items, which would be included as part of the official record and uploaded to
the City’s website. She also assured the community that the City of Irvine was adhering
to the Governor’s Executive Order in the Council Chamber and throughout City Hall by
sanitizing surfaces and equipment, as well as wearing face masks.

Mayor Khan also announced that general public comments for the City Council on items
not on the agenda would be considered at approximately 6:30 p.m.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  2
 City Council Minutes  February 9, 2021

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Vice Mayor Kim led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  INVOCATION

  Reverend Ralph E. Williamson from Christ Our Redeemer AME Church provided the
  invocation.

  Following the Invocation, Mayor Khan reordered the agenda to consider City Council
  Recognition Item No. 2.2 prior to Item No. 2.1.

  2.  CITY COUNCIL RECOGNITIONS

  2.1  Proclaim February 11, 2021, as “Irvine 2/11 Marine Battalion Day”

  This item was considered following City Council Recognition Item No.
  2.2.

  Mayor Khan presented a proclamation recognizing February 11, 2021,
  as “Irvine 2/11 Marine Battalion Day” in support of not only the 2/11
  Marines, but all of the men and women in the military who have honorably
  served, and continue to serve, in the Armed Forces; and further
  acknowledged Irvine 2/11 Marine Adoption Committee members who
  have provided years of charitable support and services benefitting United
  States Marines and their families, and the continued partnership between
  the City and the 2/11 Marine Battalion since 2007.

  Vice Mayor Kim also expressed her appreciation to the Second Battalion
  11th Marine Regiment 1st Marine Division members who served in the
  Korean War, as well as the Korean-Demilitarized Zone from July 1953 to
  1955.

  2.2  Proclaim February 2021 as “Black History Month”

  This item was considered prior to City Council Recognition Item No. 2.1.

  Mayor Khan presented a proclamation in recognition of February 2021
  as “Black History Month,” which celebrates the rich contributions made
  by Black Americans to the social, cultural, and economic vibrancy of the
  United States and Irvine. Reverend Ralph E. Williamson from Christ Our
  Redeemer AME Church expressed his appreciation for the proclamation.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  3
 City Council Minutes  February 9, 2021

  INTERIM CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  There was no report.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Councilmember Agran noted that he had received several calls from community
  members who had attempted to secure COVID-19 vaccination appointments, and that
  while the City had not been successful in securing the Orange County Great Park as a
  vaccination site, the Interim City Manager had confirmed that the City was fully prepared
  to make the Orange County Great Park available as a vaccination site within 48 hours if
  requested. He also noted that Mayor Khan had met with a local delegation from the State
  Assembly and State Senate regarding the progress of the Veterans’ Cemetery.

  In recognition of Black History Month and Irvine 2/11 Marine Battalion Day,
  Councilmember Kuo recognized Lieutenant Colonel Caleb Hyatt, previous Commanding
  Officer of the Irvine 2/11 Battalion, as he stood by Washington Headquarters Services
  Director, David Muir, on January 22, where he swore in Lloyd Austin III as the first
  African-American Secretary of Defense.

  Mayor Khan made the following announcements:

  •  For the fourth straight year, the City of Irvine ranked No. 1 in fiscal strength across
  the country. The ranking of America’s largest 75 cities calculated how a city would
  fare financially after all bills are paid. Irvine was given a surplus score of $4,100
  per tax-payer, earning the distinction as the most fiscally healthy large city in the
  United States. The “Financial State of the Cities” report was created by Truth in
  Accounting, a think tank that analyzes government financial reporting. The ranking
  confirms the City’s commitment to ensuring resident tax dollars are being wisely
  managed. Maintaining a balanced budget, with the highest level of transparency,
  remained essential to the City Council. To learn more about the ranking, visit
  cityofirvine.org.

  •  The 2021 State of the City will take place on Tuesday, February 23, at 5 p.m. Due
  to COVID-19 restrictions, the address will be delivered in a combination live and
  video format, and will not be open to the public. The State of the City Address will
  offer a look back on accomplishments from 2020 and will focus on highlights and
  initiatives for 2021, including the City’s 50th anniversary. The State of the City
  Address will be available to watch on ICTV, Cox Communications Local Access
  Channel 30 and AT&T U-Verse Channel 99. It will also be live streamed online at
  cityofirvine.org/ictv and on YouTube at youtube.com/ictv30.

  •  The spring issue of Inside Irvine is being mailed to homes this week. The issue
  highlights the restoration of the Silverado Fire burn scar, features tips for living
  sustainable, provides COVID-19 updates, and more. The edition also included
  spring and summer camps, and classes for all interests and ages. All programs
  offered follow state and local guidelines to ensure the safety of participants and
  staff. To register for camps and classes, visit yourirvine.org.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  4
 City Council Minutes  February 9, 2021

  •  The COVID-19 and Business Reopening Task Forces continue to meet on a
  regular basis. The Business Reopening Task Force met last month, and the
  business community is partnering with the Irvine Cares initiative, which
  encourages everyone to take steps to prevent the spread of COVID-19 and
  advocates for safely reopening. Since the initiative launched, more than 830
  people and 82 businesses have taken the Irvine Cares pledge. To learn more and
  take the pledge, visit cityofirvine.org/irvinecares.

 City Council Minutes  February 9, 2021

  4.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  4.1  IRVINE BUSINESS COMPLEX TRAFFIC IMPROVEMENT FEE
  PROGRAM UPDATE AND PROJECT PRIORITIZATION

  This item was considered following Council Business Item No. 5.4.

  Mayor Khan opened the public hearing at 8:32 p.m.

  Lisa Thai, Supervising Transportation Analyst, presented the staff report
  and responded to questions. Jaimee Bourgeois, Deputy Director of
  Transportation, also responded to questions.

  City Council discussion included: inquiring about whether fees for the
  widening of Red Hill could be used elsewhere in the Irvine Business
  Complex (IBC) for other transportation projects; questioned whether
  other fees outside of the Red Hill widening project would fund all other
  projects in the IBC; inquired about whether other Capital Improvement
  Program projects within the IBC had deficiencies; questioned the City of
  Santa Ana’s position on the project; inquired about the details of the
  cooperative agreement; questioned whether excess fees could be used
  to expand IBC transit; inquired about whether the City was obligated to
  lower the fees; suggested that the item be continued to a future meeting
  to allow staff additional time to conduct additional research on the
  proposed fees; inquired about which commissions reviewed the
  proposed item and the respective votes taken; questioned the
  methodology used in determining the cost/benefit analysis; inquired
  about why the number of lanes on Red Hill were being reduced from six
  lanes to four; and questioned why the proposed frequency of updates
  were decreased from every two years to three.

  Jaimee Bourgeois, Deputy Director of Transportation, noted that there
  was not a demand to expand the i-Shuttle program at this time based on
  existing ridership numbers; and explained why the number of lanes were
  being reduced from six to four on Red Hill.

  Jeff Melching, City Attorney, noted that the City was only allowed to
  charge fees for projects that were going to be built, and that if the Red
  Hill widening project was removed from the program, the City would be
  required to reduce the corresponding fees.

  There were no public comments.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  6

  5.3  CONSIDERATION OF A REQUEST BY MAYOR KHAN, VICE MAYOR
  KIM, AND COUNCILMEMBERS AGRAN AND CARROLL TO
  DISCUSS THE RENAMING OF "SUICIDE HILL" IN TURTLE ROCK

  The item was agendized at the request of Mayor Khan, Vice Mayor Kim,
  and Councilmembers Agran and Carroll, who requested City Council
  consideration to rename “Suicide Hill” in Turtle Rock.

  City Council discussion included: noting support by some to retain the
  name; suggested that any renaming be as inclusive as possible;
  questioned whether “Suicide Hill” was a formal or informal designation;
  inquired about whether any suicides had taken place at the location;
  questioned whether any signage existed with the reference of “Suicide
  Hill”; and inquired about the names of the two native tribes, suggesting
  the adoption of a new name be reflective of both tribes.

  Melissa Haley, Deputy City Manager, noted that Community Services
  staff at the Portola Springs Community Center had sought guidance
  from Joyce Perry, who was in a leadership role with the local Indigenous
  community, and learned that the location was part of two native nations;
  and at Ms. Perry’s suggestion, the renaming of the site should be easy
  to pronounce by the public and respectful to both nations.

  Kevin Corrigan, Irvine high school student, spoke in support of renaming
  the location and offered a list of potential names developed by the Irvine
  youth population.

  ACTION: Moved by Vice Mayor Kim, seconded by Councilmember
  Carroll, to:

  Direct staff to continue with the formal renaming of “Suicide Hill”
  and return within sixty (60) days with recommendations.

  5.4  CONSIDERATION OF A REQUEST BY MAYOR KHAN TO ADOPT
  AN URGENCY ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING PREMIUM PAY FOR
  GROCERY WORKERS

  This item was considered prior to Public Hearing Item No. 4.1, and was
  agendized at the request of Mayor Khan, who requested City Council
  consideration to adopt an urgency ordinance establishing premium pay
  for grocery workers.

  City Council discussion included: questioning which specific types of
  establishments would be impacted by the ordinance; discussed potential
  impacts to minority owned and ethnic serving markets; noted large profits
  by certain big box retailers that have not authorized premium pay for
  grocery workers; expressed concern about some larger establishments
  not following safety measures; requested clarification on the definition of
  “retail establishment;” questioned whether establishments that already
  provide premium pay, such as Trader Joe’s, would be subject to
  additional premium pay; inquired about the pending statuses of lawsuits
  filed by the California Grocers Association against other cities that have
  adopted similar ordinances; inquired about whether the City would
  become liable for any pay if the court struck down the legality of the
  ordinance or if any immunity would be granted to the City; clarified that
  most purchases at grocery stores were not subject to sales taxes;
  expressed concern that the proposed ordinance interfered with free
  market and did not address safety; expressed concern that businesses
  could potentially pass additional costs to consumers; and noted that
  profits by majority of these types of businesses are returned to its
  employees through retirement dividends.
